literal: With her eyes having sulked indeed, she became confused, [for] embracing, more than me, she herself eagerness having experienced.
translation: She feigned anger only with her eyes and immediately lost her resolve; for she herself was far more eager for our embrace than I was.
modern: அவள் தன் கண்களால் மட்டும் ஊடல் காட்டி உடனே கலங்கினாள்; ஏனெனில், என்னை விட அவளே தழுவிக்கொள்வதில் அதிக அவசரம் கொண்டிருந்தாள்.
explanation: The heroine attempts to feign anger (sulk) to playfully delay their union, but she can only manage to show it through her eyes. She immediately loses her resolve and becomes confused because her own desire to embrace her lover is far greater than his. Her intense eagerness (vituppu) to embrace overcomes her attempt at sulking (tuni). This couplet beautifully captures the conflict between a lover's desire to play-act anger and her overwhelming passion that defeats her own game.
